content: 1. Facilities providing maternity and newborn services should actively protect, promote, and support breastfeeding through adherence to the revised Baby-Friendly Hospital Initiative (BFHI) standards. 2. The percentage of mothers of preterm and term infants who report being informed by staff about where to access breastfeeding support in their community should be at least 80%. This information is gathered through interviews with these mothers. 3. At least 80% of health professionals providing antenatal, delivery, or newborn care should report having received pre-service or in-service training on breastfeeding within the past two years. This is assessed through interviews with clinical staff. 4. At least 80% of health professionals should report undergoing competency assessments in breastfeeding within the past two years. This is also evaluated through interviews with clinical staff. 5. At least 80% of health professionals providing antenatal, delivery, or newborn care should be able to correctly answer at least three out of four questions on breastfeeding knowledge and skills to support breastfeeding. This is determined through interviews with clinical staff. 6. The percentage of infants aged 0–5 months who were exclusively breastfed (received only breast milk) during the previous day should be monitored. This data is collected through household surveys such as MICS (Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys) or DHS (Demographic and Health Surveys). 7. The percentage of births occurring in facilities designated as Baby-Friendly (those that have passed external assessments or met compliance with BFHI standards within the past five years) should be tracked. This information is obtained from program implementation reports or national databases. 8. The percentage of mothers who received antenatal counseling on breastfeeding should be monitored. This data can be collected through household surveys, health management information systems (HMIS), exit interviews, or facility surveys. 9. The percentage of mothers who had skin-to-skin contact with their baby immediately or within five minutes after birth, lasting for at least one hour, should be recorded. This data is gathered through household surveys, HMIS, exit interviews, or facility surveys. 10. The percentage of mothers who initiated breastfeeding within one hour after birth should be tracked. This information is collected through household surveys, HMIS, exit interviews, or facility surveys. 11. The percentage of mothers who received support in learning to breastfeed after delivery should be monitored. This data is obtained through household surveys, HMIS, exit interviews, or facility surveys. 12. The percentage of mothers reporting that their infants received only breast milk (either from their own mother or a human milk bank) throughout their stay at a facility should be recorded. This information is gathered through household surveys, HMIS, exit interviews, or facility surveys. 13. The percentage of mothers whose babies stayed with them since birth without separation lasting more than one hour (rooming-in) should be monitored. This data is collected through household surveys, HMIS, exit interviews, or facility surveys. 14. The percentage of mothers who report being informed about where to access breastfeeding support in their community should be tracked. This information is gathered through household surveys, HMIS, exit interviews, or facility surveys. 15. The overall compliance with BFHI standards can be assessed by determining the percentage of mothers affirming at least six out of seven key breastfeeding practices. This data is collected through household surveys, HMIS, exit interviews, or facility surveys. 16. The percentage of provinces, states, or districts with regulations on Baby-Friendly standards should be monitored. This information is obtained from reports defined at the country level. 17. The percentage of newly graduated health professionals who received training on the updated BFHI standards should be tracked. This data is collected through reports defined at the country level. 18. The percentage of practicing health professionals who received in-service training on the updated BFHI standards should be monitored. This information is gathered through reports defined at the country level. 19. The percentage of facilities providing maternity and newborn services that have completed an external assessment within the past 3–5 years should be tracked. This data is collected through reports defined at the country level. 20. BFHI programmatic output indicators include the regulation of BFHI standards, pre-service training on BFHI standards, in-service training on BFHI standards, and the ongoing operation of external assessment processes. These indicators are essential for ensuring compliance and sustainability of the BFHI.
